title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 7
paragraphs: The sovereignty that had belonged to the Heraclids passed to the family of Croesus, called the Mermnadae, in the following way. Candaules — whom the Hellenes call Myrsilus — was the ruler of Sardis and a descendant of Alcaeus, son of Heracles. For Agron, the son of Ninus, son of Belus, son of Alcaeus, was the first of the Heraclids to become king of Sardis, and Candaules, the son of Myrsus, was the last. The kings of this land before Agron were descended from Lydus the son of Atys, from whom the whole people took the name Lydian, having earlier been called Meonian. From these kings the Heraclids — descended from Heracles and the slave-girl of Iardanus — inherited the throne in obedience to an oracle, and they reigned for twenty-two generations, five hundred and five years, passing the power from father to son down to Candaules, the son of Myrsus.
